mishnayos.summary: A husband may warn his wife not to be alone with a certain man. Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Yehoshua argue about how many witnesses are needed for the warning, and for seeing that she was alone with him.

chunks.en: If a man warns his wife (not to be alone with a certain man),
chunks.st: one who issues a warning to his wife
chunks.stMore: not to seclude herself with a particular man, so that if she does not heed his warning she will assume the status of a woman suspected by her husband of having been unfaithful [sota],

words.note: A husband who warns his wife not to be alone with a certain man.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer says:

chunks.en: He warns her in front of two witnesses,
chunks.st: He issues a warning to her based on, i.e., in the presence of, two
chunks.stMore: witnesses for the warning to be effective. If two witnesses were not present for the warning, she is not a sota even if two witnesses saw her seclusion with another man.

words.note: Two witnesses.

chunks.en: and he makes her drink the special water if one witness saw her alone with the man,
chunks.st: And the husband gives the bitter water to her to drink based on the testimony of one witness who saw the seclusion,

words.note: The bitter water of the sotah, which tests if she sinned.

chunks.en: or even if only he himself saw it.
chunks.st: or even based on his own
chunks.stMore: testimony that he himself saw them secluded together, as Rabbi Eliezer holds that only the warning requires witnesses, not the seclusion.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehoshua says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehoshua says:

chunks.en: He warns her in front of two witnesses,
chunks.st: He both issues a warning to her based on two witnesses

chunks.en: and makes her drink only if two witnesses saw her alone with the man.
chunks.st: and gives the bitter water to her to drink based on the testimony of two witnesses.

mishnayos.summary: This mishnah explains how a husband warns his wife. If she was then alone with that man, she is not allowed to her husband or to eat terumah until she is tested.

chunks.en: How does he warn her?
He says to her in front of two witnesses,
"Do not talk with that man."

words.note: A certain man; the husband names him.

chunks.en: If she talked with him anyway,
she is still allowed to stay with her husband,
and (if her husband is a Kohen) she may still eat terumah.

words.note: Special food given to Kohanim.

chunks.en: But if she went with him into a hidden place
and stayed with him long enough to become tamei,

words.note: Here: long enough that she might have sinned.

chunks.en: she is not allowed to her husband, and not allowed to eat terumah (until she is tested).
And if her husband dies (with no children),
she does chalitzah, and does not do yibum.

words.note: A ceremony that frees a widow from marrying her husband's brother.
Marrying the brother of a husband who died with no children.

mishnayos.summary: Some women married to Kohanim may not eat terumah because they are suspected of sinning. The mishnah also says how the husband brings his wife to beis din and then to the Beis HaMikdash.

chunks.en: And these women may not eat terumah:
a woman who says, "I am tamei to you" (she admits she sinned),

words.note: Here: forbidden to her husband because she sinned.

chunks.en: and when witnesses came and said that she is tamei,
and a woman who says, "I will not drink" (the special water),
and when her husband does not want to make her drink,
and when her husband was with her as her husband on the way (to the Beis HaMikdash).

words.note: Was with her as her husband.

chunks.en: What does he do with her?
He brings her to the beis din in his town,

words.note: Beis din, a court of Torah judges.

chunks.en: and they send two Torah scholars with him,

words.note: Torah scholars.

chunks.en: so that he will not be with her on the way.
Rabbi Yehudah says,
her husband is trusted with her (no scholars are needed).

mishnayos.summary: The woman is brought to the great beis din in Yerushalayim. The judges speak to her strongly and gently, hoping she will admit the truth so that Hashem's Name will not be erased.

chunks.he: הָיוּ מַעֲלִין אוֹתָהּ לְבֵית דִּין הַגָּדוֹל שֶׁבִּירוּשָׁלַיִם,
chunks.en: They would bring her up to the great beis din in Yerushalayim,

words.note: Beis din, a court of Torah judges.

chunks.he: וּמְאַיְּמִין עָלֶיהָ כְדֶרֶךְ שֶׁמְּאַיְּמִין עַל עֵדֵי נְפָשׁוֹת.
chunks.en: and they would warn her strongly, the way they warn witnesses in a case of life and death.

words.note: Cases where a person's life is at stake.

chunks.en: And they say to her,
"My daughter, lots of wine can make people sin,
lots of silliness can make people sin,
being young and foolish can make people sin,
bad neighbors can make people sin.
Do it for the sake of Hashem's great Name, which was written in holiness,
so that it will not be erased in the water."

words.note: Hashem's Name is written on a scroll that gets erased into the water.

chunks.he: וְאוֹמְרִים לְפָנֶיהָ דְּבָרִים שֶׁאֵינָהּ כְּדַאי לְשׁוֹמְעָן,
chunks.en: And they tell her things that are not fitting to hear,
not for her, and not for her whole family.

mishnayos.summary: If the woman admits she sinned, she leaves her husband without her kesubah money. If she says she is pure, she is brought to the Nikanor Gate, and the Kohen makes her look unpleasant.

chunks.en: If she says, "I am tamei,"
she gives up her kesubah and leaves (her husband).

words.note: She gives up.
The money a husband promises his wife in their marriage document.

chunks.en: But if she says, "I am pure,"
they bring her up to the Eastern Gate
at the entrance of the Nikanor Gate,

words.note: A famous gate in the Beis HaMikdash.

chunks.en: because there they give sotah women the water to drink,

words.note: Women their husbands suspect of sinning.

chunks.en: and they make women who had a baby pure,

words.en: the women who had a baby

chunks.en: and they make people with tzaraas pure.

words.note: People with tzaraas, a skin sickness sent as a punishment.

chunks.en: And a Kohen holds on to her clothes.
If they tear, they tear,
if they rip open, they rip open,
until her clothes come loose,
and he undoes her braided hair.
Rabbi Yehudah says,
If she looked pretty that way,
he would not do it,
and if her hair was pretty,
he would not undo it.

mishnayos.summary: The Kohen dresses the woman in black and takes off her jewelry, so she will not look nice. Women may come to watch, to learn not to sin.

chunks.en: If she was dressed in white,
he covers her in black.
If she had on gold jewelry and necklaces,
nose rings and rings,
they take them off her, so she will not look nice.
Then he brings an Egyptian rope
and ties it around her, high up.
And anyone who wants to see may come to see,
except her own servants and maids,
because they make her feel proud (and she won't admit).
And all the women may see her,
as the pasuk says:

chunks.he: וְנִוַּסְּרוּ כָּל הַנָּשִׁים וְלֹא תַעֲשֶׂינָה כְּזִמַּתְכֶנָה:
chunks.en: "All the women will learn not to do sins like yours."

mishnayos.summary: Hashem pays people back "measure for measure": the way a person acts is the way he is treated. The sotah made herself look nice to sin, so she is made to look unpleasant.

chunks.en: In the same measure that a person measures (acts),
he is measured with it (he is treated the same way).
She made herself pretty to do a sin,
so Hashem made her look ugly.

words.note: Literally "the Place," a name for Hashem.

chunks.en: She showed herself off to do a sin,
so Hashem showed her in front of everyone.
She began the sin with one part of her body first,
and then another part,
so that part is punished first,
and then the other part,
and the rest of her body does not escape.

mishnayos.summary: More examples of measure for measure: Shimshon followed his eyes and lost his eyes. Avshalom was proud of his hair and was caught by his hair, and he was punished for his sins.

chunks.en: Shimshon followed his eyes,
so the Pelishtim poked out his eyes,
as the pasuk says, "And the Pelishtim grabbed him
and poked out his eyes."
Avshalom was proud of his hair,

words.note: A son of Dovid HaMelech who rebelled against him.

chunks.en: so he was hung by his hair (caught in a tree).

chunks.he: וּלְפִי שֶׁבָּא עַל עֶשֶׂר פִּילַגְשֵׁי אָבִיו,
chunks.en: And because he sinned with ten of his father's wives,

words.note: Pilagshim, a kind of wife.

chunks.en: so ten spears were put in him,
as the pasuk says, "And they surrounded (him),
ten men who carried Yoav's weapons."

words.note: Dovid HaMelech's general.

chunks.en: And because he stole three hearts (he tricked three times):
the heart of his father,
and the heart of the beis din,
and the heart of Klal Yisrael,
as the pasuk says, "And Avshalom stole
the heart of the men of Yisrael,"
so three spears were stuck into him,
as the pasuk says, "And he took three
spears in his hand and stuck them in Avshalom's heart."

mishnayos.summary: Hashem also rewards good deeds measure for measure. Miriam waited for Moshe, so all Yisrael waited for her. Yosef buried Yaakov, Moshe took Yosef's bones, and Hashem Himself buried Moshe.

chunks.en: And it is the same with good things.
Miriam waited for Moshe for one hour (by the river),
as the pasuk says, "And his sister stood far away,"
so Klal Yisrael waited for her
seven days in the midbar,
as the pasuk says, "And the people did not
travel until Miriam came back in."
Yosef had the merit to bury his father,
and none of his brothers was greater than he,
as the pasuk says, "And Yosef went up
to bury his father,

chunks.he: וַיַּעַל עִמּוֹ גַּם רֶכֶב גַּם פָּרָשִׁים.
chunks.en: and both chariots and riders went up with him."
Who is greater for us than Yosef?
Only Moshe took care of him (of his bones).
Moshe had the merit to take Yosef's bones,
and no one in Klal Yisrael was greater than he,
as the pasuk says, "And Moshe took
the bones of Yosef with him."
Who is greater than Moshe?
Only Hashem Himself took care of him (buried him),
as the pasuk says, "And He buried him in the valley."
They did not say this about Moshe alone,
but about all the tzaddikim,
as the pasuk says, "Your righteousness will go before you,
the glory of Hashem will gather you in."

mishnayos.summary: The husband brings a special mincha offering for his wife. It is different from all other menachos: it starts in a plain basket, has no oil or levonah, and is made of barley flour.

chunks.he: הָיָה מֵבִיא אֶת מִנְחָתָהּ בְּתוֹךְ כְּפִיפָה מִצְרִית
chunks.en: He would bring her mincha offering in an Egyptian basket,
chunks.st: would bring his wife’s meal-offering to the priest in an Egyptian wicker basket made of palm branches,

words.note: A flour offering.

chunks.en: and put it on her hands to make her tired.
chunks.st: and he would place the meal-offering in her hands for her to hold throughout the ritual in order to fatigue her.
chunks.stMore: This might lead her to confess her guilt and not drink the water of a sota unnecessarily. The mishna lists differences between this meal-offering and other meal-offerings.

chunks.he: כָּל הַמְּנָחוֹת תְּחִלָּתָן וְסוֹפָן בִּכְלִי שָׁרֵת,
chunks.en: All menachos, from start to end, are in a holy kli,
chunks.st: Generally, all meal-offerings, from their beginnings, i.e., the moment they are consecrated, and until their ends, i.e., the moment they are sacrificed, must be in a service vessel.

words.note: Flour offerings.
A holy kli used in the Beis HaMikdash.

chunks.en: but this one starts in an Egyptian basket
chunks.st: But in the case of this one, its beginning is in a wicker basket

chunks.en: and only at the end is in a holy kli.
chunks.st: and only at its end, immediately before it is offered, is it placed in a service vessel.

chunks.en: All menachos need oil and levonah,
chunks.st: All other meal-offerings require oil and frankincense,

words.note: A sweet-smelling spice.

chunks.he: וְזוֹ אֵינָהּ טְעוּנָה לֹא שֶׁמֶן וְלֹא לְבֹנָה.
chunks.en: but this one needs no oil and no levonah.
chunks.st: and this one requires neither oil nor frankincense.

chunks.en: All menachos come from wheat,
chunks.st: Furthermore, all other meal-offerings are brought from wheat,

chunks.en: but this one comes from barley.
chunks.st: and this one is brought from barley.

chunks.he: מִנְחַת הָעֹמֶר אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁבָּאָה
chunks.en: Even though the omer offering
chunks.st: Although in fact the omer meal-offering is also

words.note: An offering of new barley brought on the second day of Pesach.

chunks.he: מִן הַשְּׂעוֹרִין הִיא הָיְתָה בָאָה גֶרֶשׂ,
chunks.en: also comes from barley, it was brought as fine ground grain,
chunks.st: brought from barley, it is still different in that it was brought as groats, i.e., high-quality meal.

words.note: Fine, high-quality ground grain.

chunks.en: but this one comes as plain flour.
chunks.st: The meal-offering of the sota, however, is brought as unsifted barley flour.

chunks.en: Rabban Gamliel says,
chunks.st: Rabban Gamliel says: This hints that

chunks.en: Just as she acted like an animal,
chunks.st: just as her actions of seclusion with another man were the actions of an animal,

chunks.en: so her korban is animal food.
chunks.st: so too her offering is animal food, i.e., barley and not wheat.

mishnayos.summary: The Kohen prepares the water for the sotah. He puts water from the kiyor into a new clay cup, and adds some earth from under a marble tile in the Heichal.

chunks.he: הָיָה מֵבִיא פְיָלִי שֶׁל חֶרֶס חֲדָשָׁה,
chunks.en: He would bring a new clay cup,
chunks.st: would bring an earthenware drinking vessel [peyalei]

chunks.en: and put into it half a log
chunks.st: and he would pour into it half a log

words.note: A measure, about the size of six eggs.

chunks.en: of water from the kiyor.
chunks.st: of water from the basin in the Temple.

words.note: The copper washing basin in the Beis HaMikdash.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says: The priest would pour only

chunks.en: "A quarter (of a log)." Just as he makes the writing less,
chunks.st: a quarter-log of water. Just as Rabbi Yehuda minimizes the writing,
chunks.stMore: as he requires that less be written on the scroll of the sota than do the Rabbis,

chunks.en: so he makes the water less.
chunks.st: so too he minimizes the amount of water
chunks.stMore: to be taken from the basin for the erasing of the text.

chunks.en: The Kohen went into the Heichal and turned to his right.
chunks.st: The priest would enter the Sanctuary and turn to his right.

words.note: The holy building of the Beis HaMikdash.

chunks.he: וּמָקוֹם הָיָה שָׁם אַמָּה עַל אַמָּה,
chunks.en: There was a spot there, an amah by an amah,
chunks.st: And there was a place there, on the Sanctuary floor, with an area of a cubit by a cubit,

words.note: A measure, about the length of an arm.

chunks.en: with a marble tile,
chunks.st: and a marble tablet [tavla] was there,

chunks.en: and a ring was fixed into it.
chunks.st: and a ring was fastened to the tablet to assist the priest

chunks.en: When he lifts it up,
chunks.st: when he would raise it.

chunks.en: he takes earth from under it and puts it in,
chunks.st: And the priest would take loose dust from underneath it and place the dust into the vessel with the water,

chunks.en: so that it can be seen on the water,
chunks.st: so that the dust would be visible upon the water,

chunks.en: as the pasuk says, "And from the earth
chunks.st: as it is stated: “And the priest shall take holy water in an earthen vessel; and of the dust

chunks.en: that is on the floor of the Mishkan,
chunks.st: that is on the floor of the Tabernacle

chunks.en: the Kohen shall take, and put it into the water."
chunks.st: the priest shall take, and put it into the water” (Numbers 5:17).

mishnayos.summary: The Kohen writes a special scroll with some of the pesukim about the sotah, to be erased in the water. The Tanna'im argue about which words he writes.

chunks.en: When he comes to write the scroll,
from which place does he write?
From the pasuk "If no
man was with you," and so on,

chunks.he: וְאַתְּ כִּי שָׂטִית תַּחַת אִישֵׁךְ וְגוֹ'.
chunks.en: and "But if you went astray while married to your husband," and so on.
He does not write "And the Kohen shall make
the woman swear," and so on.
But he does write "Hashem will make you
a curse and an oath," and so on,
"And this water that brings the curse will go into your insides
to make the stomach swell and the thigh fall."

chunks.he: וְאֵינוֹ כוֹתֵב וְאָמְרָה הָאִשָּׁה אָמֵן אָמֵן.
chunks.en: But he does not write "And the woman shall say, Amen, amen."
Rabbi Yosei says,
He did not skip anything.
Rabbi Yehudah says,
He writes nothing at all
except "Hashem will make you a curse
and an oath," and so on, "And this water that brings the curse
will go into your insides," and so on.

chunks.he: וְאֵינוֹ כוֹתֵב וְאָמְרָה הָאִשָּׁה אָמֵן אָמֵן:
chunks.en: And he does not write "And the woman shall say, Amen, amen."

mishnayos.summary: The scroll of the sotah must be written on parchment with ink that can be erased, because the Torah says it must be "in a book" and then erased.

chunks.he: אֵינוֹ כוֹתֵב לֹא עַל הַלּוּחַ וְלֹא
chunks.en: He does not write it on a board, nor
chunks.st: does not write the scroll of the sota upon a wooden tablet,

chunks.en: on paper, nor on diftera,
chunks.st: and not upon paper made from grass, and not upon diftera,
chunks.stMore: a hide that is only partially processed, as it is salted and treated with flour but not gallnuts;

words.note: Animal skin that was not fully made into parchment.

chunks.en: but only on a scroll,
chunks.st: rather, it must be written only on a scroll of parchment,

chunks.en: as the pasuk says, "in a book."
chunks.st: as it is stated: “And the priest shall write these curses in a scroll” (Numbers 5:23).

chunks.en: And he does not write with komos, nor
chunks.st: And the scribe may not write with gum [komos],

words.note: A kind of gum.

chunks.en: with kankantom, nor with anything that leaves a mark,
chunks.st: and not with iron sulfate [kankantom], nor with any substance that makes a mark and cannot be completely erased,

words.note: A kind of dye that can't be erased.

chunks.en: but only with ink,
chunks.st: but only with ink made from soot,

chunks.en: as the pasuk says, "And he shall erase,"
chunks.st: as it is stated in the continuation of the same verse: “And he shall blot
chunks.stMore: them out into the water of bitterness” (Numbers 5:23).

chunks.en: which means writing that can be erased.
chunks.st: This indicates that the scroll must be written with a writing that can be erased in water.

mishnayos.summary: The woman answers "Amen, amen" to the oath. The mishnah explains everything that her "amen" includes.

chunks.he: עַל מַה הִיא אוֹמֶרֶת אָמֵן אָמֵן.
chunks.en: About what does she say "Amen, amen"?
Amen on the curse,
amen on the oath.
Amen about this man,
amen about another man.
Amen that I did not go astray when I was engaged,

words.note: Arusah: after kiddushin, before the chuppah.

chunks.en: or married, or waiting for yibum, or married through yibum.

words.note: Her late husband's brother, who may marry her through yibum.

chunks.en: Amen that I did not become tamei.
And if I did become tamei,
let them (the curses) come upon me.
Rabbi Meir says,
Amen that I did not become tamei (before),
amen that I will not become tamei (later).

mishnayos.summary: The husband cannot add to her oath things from before she married him or after a divorce. The rule: he can only add things that would make her forbidden to him.

chunks.en: All agree that he does not add to her oath
about the time before she was engaged to him, nor
about the time after she is divorced.

chunks.he: נִסְתְּרָה לְאַחֵר וְנִטְמֵאת וְאַחַר כָּךְ הֶחֱזִירָהּ,
chunks.en: If (while divorced) she was alone with another man and became tamei, and then he took her back,
he could not add that to her oath.
This is the rule:

chunks.he: כֹּל שֶׁתִּבָּעֵל וְלֹא הָיְתָה אֲסוּרָה לוֹ,
chunks.en: Anything she did that would not make her forbidden to him,
he does not add to her oath.

mishnayos.summary: The Kohen takes the woman's mincha out of the basket, puts it into a holy kli, and places it on her hand. Then he puts his hand under hers and waves it.

chunks.he: הָיָה נוֹטֵל אֶת מִנְחָתָהּ מִתּוֹךְ כְּפִיפָה מִצְרִית
chunks.en: He would take her mincha out of the Egyptian basket
chunks.st: He would take her meal-offering out of the Egyptian wicker basket made of palm leaves in which it was lying

chunks.en: and put it into a holy kli,
chunks.st: and would put it into a service vessel

chunks.en: and put it on her hand.
chunks.st: and then place it on her hand.

chunks.en: And the Kohen puts his hand under hers and waves it.
chunks.st: And the priest would then place his hand underneath hers and wave it together with her.

mishnayos.summary: The Kohen offers the woman's mincha. The Tanna'im argue whether he first makes her drink the water or first brings the mincha, but either way it is kosher.

chunks.en: He waved it and brought it near (the mizbe'ach),
chunks.st: waved it and brought it near to the southwest corner of the altar,

chunks.en: took a handful and burned it,
chunks.st: removed a handful from it, and burned the handful;

chunks.en: and the rest is eaten by the Kohanim.
chunks.st: and the remainder was eaten by the priests.

chunks.en: He would make her drink, and after that
chunks.st: The priest would force the woman to drink the bitter water of a sota, and afterward

chunks.en: bring her mincha.
chunks.st: he would sacrifice her meal-offering.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon says:

chunks.he: מַקְרִיב אֶת מִנְחָתָהּ וְאַחַר כָּךְ הָיָה מַשְׁקָהּ,
chunks.en: He brings her mincha first, and after that he makes her drink,
chunks.st: The priest would sacrifice her meal-offering and afterward he would force her to drink,

chunks.en: as the pasuk says, "And after, he shall make
chunks.st: as it is stated:
chunks.stMore: “And the priest shall take a handful of the meal-offering, as the memorial part of it, and burn it upon the altar,

chunks.en: the woman drink the water."
chunks.st: and afterward he shall make the woman drink the water” (Numbers 5:26).

chunks.en: But if he made her drink first, and after that
chunks.st: But Rabbi Shimon concedes that if the priest first forced her to drink

chunks.en: brought her mincha, it is still kosher.
chunks.st: and afterward sacrificed her meal-offering, it is still valid.

mishnayos.summary: What happens if the woman refuses to drink: before the scroll is erased, she does not have to drink. Once it is erased, she must drink, unless she admits she sinned.

chunks.en: If, before the scroll was erased,
chunks.st: before the scroll was erased

chunks.en: she said, "I will not drink,"
chunks.st: she said: I will not drink,

chunks.en: her scroll is put away,
chunks.st: the scroll that was written for her is sequestered,

words.note: Hidden away, because Hashem's Name is written on it.

chunks.en: and her mincha is scattered on the ash pile.
chunks.st: and her meal-offering is burned and scattered over the place of the ashes,

chunks.en: Her scroll may not be used to make
chunks.st: and her scroll is not fit to give

chunks.en: another sotah drink.
chunks.st: to another sota to drink.

chunks.en: If the scroll was erased and she said, "I am tamei,"
chunks.st: If the scroll was erased and afterward she said: I am defiled,

chunks.he: הַמַּיִם נִשְׁפָּכִין וּמִנְחָתָהּ מִתְפַּזֶּרֶת עַל הַדָּשֶׁן.
chunks.en: the water is spilled out, and her mincha is scattered on the ash pile.
chunks.st: the water is poured out, and her meal-offering is scattered in the place of the ashes.

chunks.en: If the scroll was erased and she said, "I will not drink,"
chunks.st: If the scroll was already erased and she said: I will not drink,

chunks.he: מְעַרְעֲרִים אוֹתָהּ וּמַשְׁקִין אוֹתָהּ בְּעַל כָּרְחָהּ:
chunks.en: they force her to drink, even against her will.
chunks.st: she is forced to drink against her will.

mishnayos.summary: The water shows its power on a guilty woman right away, unless a zechus (merit) holds it off. The Tanna'im also argue about teaching Torah to girls, and list kinds of people who ruin the world.

chunks.he: אֵינָהּ מַסְפֶּקֶת לִשְׁתּוֹת עַד שֶׁפָּנֶיהָ מוֹרִיקוֹת
chunks.en: She does not even finish drinking before her face turns green,
and her body begins to change,
and the people say, "Take her out, take her out,
so that she will not make the Azarah tamei."

words.note: The courtyard of the Beis HaMikdash.

chunks.en: If she has a zechus,

words.note: A merit from good deeds.

chunks.en: it holds off (the punishment) for her.
Some zechus holds it off for one year,
some zechus holds it off for two years,
some zechus holds it off for three years.
From here Ben Azzai says,

words.note: A great Tanna.

chunks.he: חַיָּב אָדָם לְלַמֵּד אֶת בִּתּוֹ תוֹרָה,
chunks.en: A person must teach his daughter Torah,
so that if she drinks,
she will know that a zechus is holding it off for her.
Rabbi Eliezer says,
Anyone who teaches his daughter Torah,
it is as if he teaches her tiflus (ways that lead to sin).

words.note: Ways that lead to sin.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehoshua says,
A woman would rather have one kav (of food) and be close with her husband

words.note: A small measure of food.

chunks.en: than nine kav and be kept apart.
He used to say,
A foolish pious man,
a sly wicked man,
a woman who keeps apart too much,
and those who hurt themselves to look holy,

words.note: People who act as if they are extra holy.

chunks.en: these people ruin the world.

mishnayos.summary: Rabbi Shimon says a zechus does not hold off the water, because then people would doubt the water and the innocent women. Rebbi says it does hold it off, but the woman slowly gets weaker.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon says:

chunks.en: A zechus does not hold off the bitter water.
chunks.st: Merit does not delay the punishment of the bitter water of a sota,

chunks.en: And if you say
chunks.st: and if you say that

chunks.en: that a zechus holds off the water that brings the curse,
chunks.st: merit does delay the punishment of the water that causes the curse, as stated earlier by the Rabbis (20a),

chunks.en: you make the water weak
chunks.st: you weaken [madhe] the power of the bitter water

chunks.en: in the eyes of all the women who drink,
chunks.st: before all the women who drink
chunks.stMore: the water, who will no longer be afraid of it, as they will rely on their merit to save them.

chunks.en: and you give a bad name
chunks.st: And you defame

chunks.en: to the pure women who drank,
chunks.st: the untainted women who drank the water and survived,

chunks.en: since people will say, "They are tamei, but
chunks.st: as people say: They are defiled but

chunks.en: a zechus held it off for them."
chunks.st: it is their merit that delayed the punishment for them.

chunks.en: Rebbi says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi says:

words.note: Rabbi Yehudah HaNasi, who put together the Mishnah.

chunks.en: A zechus does hold off the water that brings the curse,
chunks.st: Merit delays the punishment of the water that causes the curse,

chunks.en: but she does not have children and does not grow stronger.
chunks.st: but a woman whose punishment is delayed does not give birth and does not flourish;

chunks.en: Instead, she gets weaker and weaker,
chunks.st: rather, she progressively deteriorates.

chunks.en: and in the end she dies the same death.
chunks.st: Ultimately she dies by the same death as a sota who dies immediately.

mishnayos.summary: If the sotah's mincha becomes tamei, it is treated like any other mincha. The mishnah lists when her mincha must be burned instead of eaten.

chunks.he: נִטְמֵאת מִנְחָתָהּ עַד שֶׁלֹּא קָדְשָׁה בַכְּלִי,
chunks.en: If her mincha became tamei before it became holy in the kli,
it is like all menachos, and it is redeemed.

words.note: Exchanged for money, so it is no longer holy.

chunks.en: But if after it became holy in the kli,
it is like all menachos, and it is burned.
And these are the women whose menachos are burned:
a woman who says, "I am tamei to you,"
and when witnesses came about her that she is tamei,
and one who says, "I will not drink,"
and when her husband does not want to make her drink,
and when her husband was with her as her husband on the way.
And all women married to Kohanim,
their menachos are burned.

mishnayos.summary: The mishnah lists ways a Kohen and a Kohen's daughter are different: whose mincha is eaten, who can lose the holiness of kehunah, who may become tamei to the dead, and who eats kodshei kodashim.

chunks.en: A Yisrael woman who married a Kohen,
her mincha is burned.
A Kohen's daughter who married a Yisrael,
her mincha is eaten.
What is the difference between a Kohen and a Kohen's daughter?
A Kohen's daughter's mincha is eaten,
but a Kohen's mincha is not eaten.
A Kohen's daughter can lose her special holiness,
but a Kohen does not lose his.
A Kohen's daughter may become tamei to the dead,
but a Kohen may not become tamei to the dead.
A Kohen eats kodshei kodashim,

words.note: Kodshei kodashim, the holiest korbanos.

chunks.en: but a Kohen's daughter does not eat kodshei kodashim.

mishnayos.summary: The mishnah lists halachos that are different for a man and for a woman, such as a metzora's mourning signs, nezirus for a child, and punishments of beis din.

chunks.en: What is the difference between a man and a woman?
A man (who is a metzora) lets his hair grow and tears his clothes,
but a woman does not let her hair grow or tear her clothes.
A man can make his young son a nazir,

words.note: A person who promises not to drink wine or cut his hair.

chunks.he: וְאֵין הָאִשָּׁה מַדֶּרֶת אֶת בְּנָהּ בְּנָזִיר.
chunks.en: but a woman cannot make her son a nazir.
A man can finish his nezirus with his father's nezirus korbanos,

chunks.he: וְאֵין הָאִשָּׁה מְגַלַּחַת עַל נְזִירוּת אָבִיהָ.
chunks.en: but a woman cannot finish hers with her father's nezirus korbanos.
A man can sell his young daughter (as a maidservant),
but a woman cannot sell her daughter.
A man can give his young daughter in marriage,
but a woman cannot give her daughter in marriage.
A man is stoned without his clothes,
but a woman is not stoned without her clothes.
A man is hung (after being stoned),
but a woman is not hung.
A man is sold (as a servant) for his stealing,
but a woman is not sold for her stealing.

mishnayos.summary: Some women do not drink the sotah water and do not get their kesubah: an arusah, a woman waiting for yibum, and women in a marriage that the Torah does not allow.

chunks.en: An arusah and a woman waiting for yibum

words.note: Arusah: after kiddushin, before the chuppah.
Her late husband's brother, who may marry her through yibum.

chunks.en: do not drink, and do not get their kesubah,
as the pasuk says,
"When a wife goes astray while under her husband,"
leaving out an arusah and one waiting for yibum.
A widow married to a Kohen Gadol,

words.note: The High Priest.

chunks.en: a divorced woman or a chalutzah married to a regular Kohen,

words.note: A woman freed from yibum by chalitzah.

chunks.en: a mamzeres or a nesinah married to a Yisrael,

words.note: A girl born from a forbidden relationship.
A girl from the Givonim, who joined Klal Yisrael in Yehoshua's time.

chunks.en: or a Yisrael woman married to a mamzer or a nasin:
they do not drink and do not get their kesubah.

mishnayos.summary: More women who do not drink: some lose their kesubah, and some still get it because it is their husband's doing. Beis Shammai and Beis Hillel argue about a woman whose husband died first.

chunks.he: וְאֵלּוּ לֹא שׁוֹתוֹת וְלֹא נוֹטְלוֹת כְּתֻבָּה.
chunks.en: And these women do not drink and do not get their kesubah:
one who says, "I am tamei,"
and when witnesses came about her that she is tamei,
and one who says, "I will not drink."
If her husband said, "I will not make her drink,"
or her husband was with her as her husband on the way,
she gets her kesubah and does not drink.
If their husbands died before they drank,
Beis Shammai say,
They get their kesubah and do not drink.
And Beis Hillel say,
They do not drink, and they do not get their kesubah.

mishnayos.summary: Rabbi Meir and the Sages argue about a woman who married while expecting or nursing another man's baby, and Rabbi Eliezer argues about a woman who cannot have children. All other women either drink or lose their kesubah.

chunks.en: A woman expecting another man's baby, or nursing another man's baby,
does not drink and does not get her kesubah.
That is what Rabbi Meir says.
But the Sages say,

chunks.he: יָכוֹל הוּא לְהַפְרִישָׁהּ וּלְהַחֲזִירָהּ לְאַחַר זְמַן.
chunks.en: He can separate from her and take her back after the time is over.
An aylonis, an old woman, and a woman who cannot have children

words.note: A woman who cannot have children.

chunks.en: do not drink and do not get their kesubah.
Rabbi Eliezer says,
He can marry another woman
and have children with her.
And all other women

chunks.he: אוֹ שׁוֹתוֹת אוֹ לֹא נוֹטְלוֹת כְּתֻבָּה:
chunks.en: either drink, or do not get their kesubah.

mishnayos.summary: A Kohen's wife and a saris's wife also drink. A husband may warn his wife about any man, even relatives, except for a young boy.

chunks.en: A Kohen's wife drinks, and (if she is innocent) she is allowed to her husband.
The wife of a saris drinks.

words.note: A man who cannot have children.

chunks.en: A husband may warn her about any man, even close relatives,

words.note: Relatives she could never marry.

chunks.en: except for a young boy,
and except for one who is not a man.

mishnayos.summary: When a husband cannot warn his wife (he became deaf, lost his mind, or is in jail), beis din warns her. Rabbi Yosei says she can even be made to drink later.

chunks.en: And these are the women whom beis din warns:
chunks.st: And these are the women to whom the court issues a warning in place of their husbands:

words.note: Beis din, a court of Torah judges.

chunks.en: a woman whose husband became deaf or lost his mind,
chunks.st: One whose husband became a deaf-mute or became an imbecile,

chunks.en: or was locked up in jail.
chunks.st: or was incarcerated in prison.

chunks.en: They did not say this to make her drink,
chunks.st: The Sages said that the court warns her not in order to have her drink the bitter water if she disobeys the warning,

chunks.en: but to make her lose her kesubah.
chunks.st: but in order to disqualify her from receiving payment of her marriage contract.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei says: The court’s warning

chunks.en: Also to make her drink:
chunks.st: also serves to have her drink,

chunks.en: when her husband gets out of jail, he makes her drink.
chunks.st: and when her husband is released from prison he has her drink.

mishnayos.summary: The water checks both the woman and the other man. Rabbi Akiva and Rebbi learn from extra words in the pesukim that she becomes forbidden both to her husband and to the other man.

chunks.en: Just as the water checks her,
so the water checks him (the other man),
as the pasuk says "And it shall come," and again "And it shall come."
Just as she is forbidden to her husband,
so she is forbidden to the other man,
as the pasuk says "she became tamei"
and "and she became tamei." That is what Rabbi Akiva says.
Rabbi Yehoshua said,

chunks.he: כָּךְ הָיָה דוֹרֵשׁ זְכַרְיָה בֶן הַקַּצָּב.
chunks.en: This is how Zecharyah ben HaKatzav used to explain it.
Rebbi says,

words.note: Rabbi Yehudah HaNasi, who put together the Mishnah.

chunks.en: The two times it is said in the parashah,
"she became tamei," "she became tamei" —
one is for the husband, and one is for the other man.

mishnayos.summary: Rabbi Akiva taught from a pasuk that a loaf on the second level of tumah can make another loaf tamei on the third level. Rabbi Yehoshua wished his rebbi, Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai, could have heard it.

chunks.en: On that day Rabbi Akiva explained:
chunks.st: On that same day that Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya was appointed head of the Sanhedrin, Rabbi Akiva interpreted the verse: “

chunks.en: "And every clay kli
chunks.st: And every earthen vessel

chunks.en: that one of them falls into,
chunks.st: into which any of them falls,

chunks.en: everything inside it yitma (will be tamei)."
chunks.st: whatever is in it shall be impure [yitma],
chunks.stMore: and you shall break it” (Leviticus 11:33), as follows:

chunks.en: It does not say "tamei," but "yitma,"
chunks.st: The verse does not state: Is impure [tamei], but rather: “Shall be impure,”

chunks.en: to teach that it makes other things tamei.
chunks.st: in order to indicate that not only does the vessel itself become ritually impure, but it can now render other items ritually impure.

chunks.en: This teaches about a loaf that is a sheini (on the second level),
chunks.st: This teaches with regard to a loaf that has second-
chunks.stMore: degree ritual impurity status due to its being placed inside an earthenware vessel that had first-degree impurity,

words.note: A sheini: tamei on the second level.

chunks.en: that it makes a third one tamei.
chunks.st: that it can render other food with which it comes into contact impure with third-degree impurity status.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehoshua said,
chunks.st: After hearing Rabbi Akiva’s statement, Rabbi Yehoshua said:

chunks.en: "Who will take the dust off your eyes,
chunks.st: Who will remove the dirt from your eyes,

chunks.en: Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai!
chunks.st: Rabban Yoḥanan ben Zakkai, so that you could live and see this?

chunks.en: For you used to say,
chunks.st: As you would say:

chunks.he: עָתִיד דּוֹר אַחֵר לְטַהֵר כִּכָּר שְׁלִישִׁי,
chunks.en: 'Some day, another generation will say a third-level loaf is tahor,
chunks.st: In the future, another generation is destined to deem pure a loaf that contracted third-degree impurity,

chunks.he: שֶׁאֵין לוֹ מִקְרָא מִן הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁהוּא טָמֵא.
chunks.en: because there is no pasuk in the Torah that says it is tamei.'
chunks.st: as there is no explicit verse from the Torah stating that it is impure.

chunks.en: But here is Akiva, your student, bringing
chunks.st: But now Rabbi Akiva, your disciple, brings

chunks.en: a pasuk from the Torah that it is tamei,
chunks.st: a verse from the Torah indicating that it is impure,

chunks.en: as it says, 'Whatever is inside it yitma.'"
chunks.st: as it is stated: “Whatever is in it shall be impure.”

mishnayos.summary: Two pesukim give different sizes for the land around the cities of the Leviim. Rabbi Akiva explains that the extra two thousand amos teach the techum of Shabbos, and Rabbi Eliezer says they are fields and vineyards.

chunks.en: On that day Rabbi Akiva explained:
chunks.st: on that same day Rabbi Akiva interpreted the verses with regard to the Levite cities as follows: One verse states: “

chunks.en: "And you shall measure outside the city
chunks.st: And you shall measure outside the city

chunks.he: אֶת פְּאַת קֵדְמָה אַלְפַּיִם בָּאַמָּה וְגוֹ',
chunks.en: on the east side two thousand amos," and so on.
chunks.st: for the east side two thousand cubits…
chunks.stMore: this shall be for them the open land outside the cities” (Numbers 35:5),

chunks.en: And another pasuk says,
chunks.st: and another verse states:
chunks.stMore: “And the open land around the cities, which you shall give to the Levites, shall be

chunks.he: מִקִּיר הָעִיר וָחוּצָה אֶלֶף אַמָּה סָבִיב.
chunks.en: "from the wall of the city outward, a thousand amos all around."
chunks.st: from the wall of the city and outward one thousand cubits round about” (Numbers 35:4).

chunks.en: We cannot say a thousand amos,
chunks.st: It is impossible to say that the area around the cities given to the Levites was only one thousand cubits,

chunks.en: since it already says two thousand amos.
chunks.st: as it is already stated: “Two thousand cubits.”

chunks.en: And we cannot say two thousand amos,
chunks.st: And it is impossible to say that two thousand cubits were left for them,

chunks.en: since it already says a thousand amos.
chunks.st: as it is already stated: “One thousand cubits.”

chunks.en: So how does it work?
chunks.st: How can these texts be reconciled?

chunks.en: A thousand amos are open land around the city,
chunks.st: One thousand cubits are to be set aside as a tract of open land surrounding the city,

words.note: Open land around a city of the Leviim.

chunks.en: and two thousand amos are the techum of Shabbos.
chunks.st: and the two thousand cubits are mentioned not in order to be given to the Levites, but to indicate the boundary of the Shabbat limit,
chunks.stMore: beyond which it is forbidden to travel on Shabbat. This verse thereby serves as the source for the two-thousand-cubit Shabbat limit.

words.note: Techum: how far one may walk outside a city on Shabbos.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer, the son of
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer, son of

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei HaGelili, says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei HaGelili, says otherwise:

chunks.en: A thousand amos are open land,
chunks.st: One thousand cubits were given to the Levites as an open tract
chunks.stMore: of land, that could not be planted or built upon,

chunks.en: and two thousand amos are for fields and vineyards.
chunks.st: and two thousand cubits of additional land were given to the Levites for planting fields and vineyards.

mishnayos.summary: Rabbi Akiva learns from the word "saying" that at the Yam Suf, Klal Yisrael answered after Moshe on every line of the Shirah, like Hallel. Rabbi Nechemyah says they sang it together, like Shema.

chunks.he: בּוֹ בַיּוֹם דָּרַשׁ רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא (שמות טו),
chunks.en: On that day Rabbi Akiva explained:
chunks.st: on that same day Rabbi Akiva interpreted the verse:

chunks.en: "Then Moshe and Bnei Yisrael sang
chunks.st: “Then Moses and the children of Israel sang

chunks.en: this song to Hashem,
chunks.st: this song to the Lord,

chunks.en: and they said, saying."
chunks.st: and said, saying” (Exodus 15:1), as follows:

chunks.en: There was no need to say "saying,"
chunks.st: As there is no need for the verse to state the word “saying,”
chunks.stMore: because it states the word “said” immediately prior to it,

chunks.en: so why does it say "saying"?
chunks.st: why must the verse state the word “saying”?

chunks.he: מְלַמֵּד שֶׁהָיוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל עוֹנִין אַחֲרָיו שֶׁל משֶׁה
chunks.en: It teaches that Klal Yisrael answered after Moshe
chunks.st: It teaches that the Jewish people would repeat in song after Moses

chunks.en: on every single line,
chunks.st: every single statement he said,

chunks.en: like when we say Hallel.
chunks.st: as is done when reciting hallel. After Moses would recite a verse, they would say as a refrain: “I will sing to the Lord, for He is highly exalted” (Exodus 15:1). It is

chunks.en: That is why it says "saying."
chunks.st: for this reason that the word “saying” is stated, in addition to the word “said.”

chunks.en: Rabbi Nechemyah says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Neḥemya says: The people sang the song together with Moses

chunks.en: Like when we say Shema,
chunks.st: as is done when reciting Shema,
chunks.stMore: which is recited in unison after the prayer leader begins,

chunks.en: and not like when we say Hallel.
chunks.st: and not as is done when reciting hallel.

mishnayos.summary: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Hurkanos taught from the pesukim that Iyov served Hashem out of love, not only out of fear. Rabbi Yehoshua wished Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai could have heard it.

chunks.he: בּוֹ בַיּוֹם דָּרַשׁ רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן הוּרְקְנוֹס,
chunks.en: On that day Rabbi Yehoshua ben Hurkanos explained:
chunks.st: On that same day Rabbi Yehoshua ben Hyrcanus taught:

chunks.he: לֹא עָבַד אִיּוֹב אֶת הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
chunks.en: Iyov did not serve Hakadosh Baruch Hu
chunks.st: Job served the Holy One, Blessed be He,

chunks.en: except out of love,
chunks.st: only out of love,

chunks.en: as the pasuk says,
chunks.st: as it is stated:

chunks.en: "Even if He kills me, I will hope to Him."
chunks.st: “Though He will slay me, still I will trust in Him” (Job 13:15).

chunks.en: But the matter is still unclear:
chunks.st: And still, the matter is even,
chunks.stMore: i.e., the verse is ambiguous, as there are two possible interpretations of the verse.

chunks.he: לוֹ אֲנִי מְצַפֶּה אוֹ אֵינִי מְצַפֶּה,
chunks.en: does it mean "I wait for Him," or "I do not wait"?
chunks.st: Was Job saying: I will await Him, expressing his yearning for God; or should the verse be interpreted as saying I will not await
chunks.stMore: Him. As the word “lo” can mean either “to him” or “not,” it is unclear which meaning is intended here.

chunks.en: So the pasuk teaches:
chunks.st: This dilemma is resolved elsewhere, where the verse states a clearer indication of Job’s intent:

chunks.he: עַד אֶגְוָע לֹא אָסִיר תֻּמָּתִי מִמֶּנִּי,
chunks.en: "Until I die, I will not give up my innocence."
chunks.st: “Till I die I will not put away my integrity from me” (Job 27:5).

chunks.en: This teaches that he did it out of love.
chunks.st: This teaches that he acted out of love.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehoshua said,

chunks.en: If a man warned his wife and she was alone (with that man),

chunks.en: That is what Rabbi Eliezer says.
chunks.st: This is the statement of Rabbi Eliezer,
chunks.stMore: who, as quoted in the first mishna of the tractate (2a), holds that there is no necessity for witnesses to testify with regard to the seclusion, and the woman becomes forbidden to her husband even in the absence of witnesses, by the husband’s word alone.

chunks.en: If he was found hidden under a pile of stones,
chunks.st: was found concealed in a pile of stones,

chunks.en: or hanging on a tree,
chunks.st: or hanging on a tree,

chunks.en: or floating on the water,
chunks.st: or floating on the surface of the water,

chunks.st: then the judges would not break the neck of the heifer,

chunks.en: as the pasuk says, "in the land" —
chunks.st: as it is stated: “If one be found slain in the land” (Deuteronomy 21:1),

chunks.en: and not hidden under a pile;
chunks.st: and not concealed in a pile of stones;

chunks.st: “lying” on the ground and not hanging on a tree;

and the rest of him in another place,
they bring the head to the body,

chunks.st: which has not pulled a yoke.

chunks.st: it should be buried in its place.

chunks.st: and another woman says: You did not see,

chunks.st: and two witnesses say: You did not see,

chunks.en: they do the eglah arufah.

chunks.st: and one witness says to them: You did not see,

mishnayos.summary: When there were many killers, the eglah arufah stopped, and when there were many sinners, the bitter water stopped. When two great Sages died, the "eshkolos" came to an end.

chunks.en: When the killers became many,
the eglah arufah stopped.
When Eliezer ben Dinai came,
who was also called Techinah ben Perishah,
they started calling him "son of the killer."
When the sinners became many,

words.note: People who did the sin of a forbidden relationship.

chunks.en: the bitter water stopped.
Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai stopped it,
as the pasuk says (Hoshea 4):

chunks.he: לֹא אֶפְקוֹד עַל בְּנוֹתֵיכֶם כִּי תִזְנֶינָה
chunks.en: "I will not punish your daughters when they sin,
nor your daughters-in-law when they sin,
because they (the men) also..."
chunks.explain: When the husbands sin too, the wives are not tested.

chunks.he: מִשֶּׁמֵּת יוֹסֵי בֶן יוֹעֶזֶר אִישׁ צְרֵדָה
chunks.en: When Yosei ben Yoezer of Tzeredah
and Yosei ben Yochanan of Yerushalayim died,
the "eshkolos" (clusters) came to an end,
chunks.explain: A name for the greatest Sages of those times.

chunks.en: as the pasuk says (Michah 7):
"There is no cluster to eat,
no first fig that my soul wants."

mishnayos.summary: Yochanan the Kohen Gadol stopped some things that were done before him, and in his days everyone was careful to take maaser.

chunks.he: יוֹחָנָן כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל הֶעֱבִיר הוֹדָיַת הַמַּעֲשֵׂר.
chunks.en: Yochanan the Kohen Gadol stopped the declaration about maaser.
chunks.st: Yoḥanan the High Priest took away the declaration of the tithe.
chunks.stMore: After his time, no one recited the passage about the elimination of tithes that had previously been said at the end of a three-year tithing cycle.

chunks.en: He also stopped
chunks.st: He also nullified the actions of

chunks.en: the "wakers" and the "knockers."
chunks.explain: Things that were done in the Beis HaMikdash.
chunks.st: the awakeners and the strikers at the Temple.

chunks.he: עַד יָמָיו הָיָה פַטִּישׁ מַכֶּה בִירוּשָׁלַיִם.
chunks.en: Until his days, a hammer would bang in Yerushalayim (on Chol Hamoed).
chunks.st: Until his days the hammer of smiths would strike in Jerusalem
chunks.stMore: on the intermediate days of a Festival, but he banned the practice.

chunks.en: And in his days, no one needed
chunks.st: And furthermore, in his days there was no need

chunks.en: to ask about demai.
chunks.st: to inquire about doubtfully tithed produce [demai],
chunks.stMore: as everyone was careful to tithe. This mishna continues with the list of items that were nullified.

words.note: Food that may not have had maaser taken from it.

mishnayos.summary: When the Sanhedrin stopped, singing at parties with wine was stopped too.

chunks.en: When the Sanhedrin stopped,
chunks.st: From the time when the Sanhedrin ceased

chunks.en: singing stopped at parties,
chunks.st: song was also nullified from the places of feasts,

chunks.en: as the pasuk says (Yeshayahu 24):
chunks.st: as it is stated:

chunks.en: "They shall not drink wine with song..."

mishnayos.summary: After the first Nevi'im died and the Beis HaMikdash was destroyed, many good things stopped, and the world lost some of its bracha.

chunks.en: When the first Nevi'im died,
chunks.st: From the time when the early prophets died

chunks.en: the Urim VeTumim stopped.
chunks.st: the Urim VeTummim was nullified.

chunks.en: When the Beis HaMikdash was destroyed,
chunks.st: From the time when the Second Temple was destroyed

chunks.en: the shamir and the sweet honeycomb stopped,
chunks.st: the shamir worm ceased to exist and also the sweetness of the honeycomb,
chunks.stMore: as the verse says with regard to the laws of the Torah: “More to be desired are they than gold, indeed, than much fine gold; sweeter also than honey and the honeycomb” (Psalms 19:11).

words.note: A special worm.

chunks.en: and faithful people came to an end,
chunks.st: And men of faith ceased from being among the Jewish people,

chunks.en: as the pasuk says (Tehillim 12):
chunks.st: as it is stated:

chunks.he: הוֹשִׁיעָה ה' כִּי גָמַר חָסִיד וְגוֹ'.
chunks.en: "Help, Hashem, for the pious man is gone..."
chunks.st: “Help, Lord, for the pious man is finished;
chunks.stMore: for the faithful fail from among the children of men” (Psalms 12:2).

chunks.en: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel
chunks.st: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel

chunks.en: says in the name of Rabbi Yehoshua,
chunks.st: says that Rabbi Yehoshua testified:

chunks.en: From the day the Beis HaMikdash was destroyed,
chunks.st: From the day the Temple was destroyed

chunks.en: there is no day without a curse,
chunks.st: there is no day that does not include some form of curse.

chunks.en: and the dew does not come down for bracha,
chunks.st: And since then the dew has not descended for blessing,

chunks.en: and the taste was taken from fruit.
chunks.st: and the taste has been removed from fruit.

mishnayos.summary: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar and the Sages say which sins took away the good taste of fruit and grain.

chunks.he: הַטָּהֳרָה נָטְלָה אֶת הַטַּעַם וְאֶת הָרֵיחַ.
chunks.en: Losing taharah took away the taste and the smell.
Not taking maaser took away the richness of the grain.
And the Sages say,
Forbidden relationships and witchcraft finished everything.

mishnayos.summary: The mishnah tells what was lost when each great Sage died, describes the hard times before Mashiach, and ends with Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair's ladder of good traits that leads all the way to techiyas hameisim.

chunks.en: When Rabbi Meir died,
the people who told meshalim stopped.

words.note: Parables: stories that teach a lesson.

chunks.en: When Ben Azzai died,
the hard-working learners stopped.
When Ben Zoma died,
the darshanim stopped.

words.note: People who explain pesukim.

chunks.en: When Rabbi Yehoshua died,
goodness stopped from the world.
When Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel died,
locusts came and troubles grew.
When Rabbi Elazar ben Azaryah died,
the Sages stopped being rich.
When Rabbi Akiva died,
the honor of the Torah stopped.
When Rabbi Chanina ben Dosa died,
the men of wonderful deeds stopped.
When Rabbi Yosei Ketanusa died,
the chassidim stopped.

words.note: Very pious people.

chunks.en: And why was he called Ketanusa ("the small")?
Because he was the smallest of the chassidim.
When Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai died,
the shine of wisdom stopped.
When Rabban Gamliel the Elder died,

chunks.he: בָּטַל כְּבוֹד הַתּוֹרָה וּמֵתָה טָהֳרָה וּפְרִישׁוּת.
chunks.en: the honor of the Torah stopped, and purity and perishus died.

words.note: Staying away from extra pleasures.

chunks.en: When Rabbi Yishmael ben Pavi died,
the shine of the Kehunah stopped.
When Rebbi died,

words.note: Rabbi Yehudah HaNasi.

chunks.en: humility and fear of sin stopped.
Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair says,
When the Beis HaMikdash was destroyed,
the chaverim and noble people were ashamed,
and covered their heads,
and men of good deeds became fewer,
and strong-armed people and smooth talkers grew stronger,
and no one explains and no one seeks,
and no one asks.
On whom can we lean?
On our Father in Heaven.
Rabbi Eliezer HaGadol says,
From the day the Beis HaMikdash was destroyed,
the Sages began to be like teachers of children,
and the teachers like shamashim,
and shamashim like simple people,
and simple people are getting weaker and weaker,
and no one seeks.
On whom can we lean?
On our Father in Heaven.
Before Mashiach comes, chutzpah will grow,
and prices will go way up.
The vine will give its fruit, but wine will be expensive,
and the kingdom will turn away from emunah,
and no one will rebuke.
The Sages' meeting place will become a place of sin,
and the Galil will be destroyed,
and the Gavlan will be empty,
and the people of the border will go around from city to city,
and no one will be kind to them.
The wisdom of the Sages will go bad,
people who fear sin will be hated,
and truth will be missing.
Young people will embarrass old people,
old people will stand up for children.
(Michah 7) A son will shame his father,
a daughter will rise up against her mother,
a daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law,
a man's enemies will be the people of his own house.
The face of the generation will be like the face of a dog,
a son will not be ashamed before his father.
And on whom can we lean?
On our Father in Heaven.
Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair says,
Being quick (to do mitzvos) leads to being clean (from sin),
being clean leads to purity,
purity leads to perishus,
perishus leads to holiness,
holiness leads to humility,
humility leads to fear of sin,
fear of sin leads to chassidus,
chassidus leads to Ruach Hakodesh,

chunks.he: וְרוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ מְבִיאָה לִידֵי תְחִיַּת הַמֵּתִים,
chunks.en: Ruach Hakodesh leads to techiyas hameisim,
chunks.explain: Techiyas hameisim: when the dead will come back to life.
